questions.q: In Nigeria, traditional Adire fabric is famously dyed using an extract from a specific local plant to achieve its rich colour. What colour does the 'Indigo' plant produce?
questions.explain: The Indigo plant (locally known as 'Elu' among the Yoruba) is the traditional source for the rich deep blue or blue-black dye used heavily in Adire textile production.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Camwood (known as Osun or Ufie) is a local Nigerian material historically processed into a powder. What colour does it produce when used as a dye or cosmetic?
questions.explain: Camwood yields a rich red or reddish-brown pigment. It is widely used in West Africa as a local dye for fabrics and as a cosmetic for the skin.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which local plant material is commonly used in Northern Nigeria (and elsewhere) to create intricate reddish-brown or black decorative patterns on hands and feet?
questions.explain: Henna, locally known as Lali, is derived from the Lawsonia inermis plant. It leaves a temporary stain (usually reddish-brown) and is culturally popular for skin beautification during celebrations.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Chalk or Kaolin clay, known traditionally as 'Nzu' or 'Efun', is a local source for which colour used in traditional Nigerian rituals and art?
questions.explain: Kaolin clay is a soft white clay widely used across Nigeria as 'Nzu' (Igbo) or 'Efun' (Yoruba). It serves as a source of local white pigment for body painting and spiritual art.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: The traditional Igbo art form of 'Uli' involves drawing distinct lines and patterns on the human body or on building walls. What colour does the Uli dye primarily produce?
questions.explain: Uli is a dye made from the berries of certain local plants (e.g., Rothmannia) that stains the skin a deep blue-black colour, creating beautiful linear body art and murals.
